development_history.v1_observation: The v1 solver exceeded its 60000-token budget by repeatedly requesting narrow Python analyses before submission.
development_history.v2_observation: The v2 prompt reduced analysis calls, but a third-call code error produced a long tool result and the model requested a fourth repair. Prompt-only stopping was insufficient.
development_history.v3_change: The solver now enforces at most three Python calls per sample, marks the third call as final, blocks later execution, and limits each tool result replayed to the model to 2000 bytes.

primary_question: Does CARE's hypothesis-sampling, falsification, and evidence-rerouting workflow improve scientific data-analysis quality or the quality-cost frontier relative to plain ReAct under the same model, task tools, and resource limits?

arms.description: Official agent-baselines ReAct solver using the benchmark-provided tools.
Frozen CARE skill map with competing hypotheses, falsification, evidence rerouting, and the v3 controller-enforced execution policy.
CARE ablation with the rerouting node disabled.
Plain ReAct control with no CARE procedural map.

care_execution_policy.policy_role: Ablatable CARE controller component; benchmark tools and outer model budget remain matched across arms.

primary_endpoint: paired per-task difference in official DiscoveryBench HMS score: care_full minus official_react
secondary_endpoints: frozen AstaBench model cost per task

success_rules.quality_superiority: mean paired HMS difference > 0 and task-bootstrap 95% confidence interval lower bound > 0 on the untouched test split
success_rules.cost_adjusted_noninferiority: HMS difference lower bound >= -1.0 point and median frozen cost <= 80% of official_react

reporting.openness: open source and closed weights when an API model is used
